_about: Slide 5 (r-improve). Intermediate-task training: fine-tune BERT-base on MNLI first, then on RTE (STILTs, Phang et al., 2018). 5-seed numbers from results/runs.jsonl (tags repro vs mnli_inter, lr 2e-5, 3 epochs, same seeds, paired). The example pair comes from our seed-1 viz models.

rte.question: does sentence A entail sentence B? (2 classes: entailed / not entailed)

mnli.question: does A entail B, contradict it, or neither? (3 classes)

recipe: 1) fine-tune pre-trained BERT-base on MNLI (3 epochs) and save it; 2) replace its 3-way head with a new 2-way head; 3) fine-tune on RTE exactly as before (lr 2e-5, 3 epochs, batch 32)
paper_support: BERT paper, footnote 14: they 'did observe substantial improvements on RTE from multitask training with MNLI' but report no numbers
phang_2018: STILTs (Phang et al., 2018) report RTE 68.6 -> 79.1 for BERT-base with MNLI first (best of 20 restarts, not means)

example.a: Napkins, invitations and plain old paper cost more than they did a month ago.
example.b: The cost of paper is rising.
example._note: from our seed-1 models (direct: dev 60.6 in this re-run; MNLI-first: 78.0); across the 277 dev pairs MNLI-first fixes 68 pairs and breaks 20
